newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Holderbank to take over Sri Lanka firm.
newsitem.headline: Holderbank to take over Sri Lanka firm.

text.p: Holderbank Financiere Glaris Ltd has agreed to take over Sri Lanka's Puttalam Cement Co Ltd, Puttalam chairman Manilal Fernando said on Tuesday.
Holderbank, one of the world's leading cement manufacturers, has agreed with major shareholders to buy shares totalling 87.5 percent of Puttalam Cement's issued capital, he said.
"Holderbank will buy all these shares for a realistic price based on their 1993 bid price," Fernando said in an interview.

Puttalam Cement, Sri Lanka's largest and only integrated cement manufacturer, was privatised in December 1993 when the government sold a 90 percent stake in the company to a consortium of investors led by the Tawakkal Group of Pakistan for 2.03 billion rupees.

The Tawakkal Group has agreed to sell all its 34 percent stake in Puttalam to Holderbank, which is also buying 48.5 percent of Puttalam from a group of Hong Kong investors and five percent from Sri Lanka's investment bank Vanik Incorporation, Fernando said.
Holderbank was unsuccessful in its takeover bid in 1993 when it wanted to buy at around 1.2 billion rupees.
Fernando said the purchase of the 87.5 percent stake would be completed by the end of this week.
Holderbank has more than 70 integrated cement plants and about 20 grinding units worldwide, he said.
"Despite it being three years since they first showed interest, Holderbank still sees Sri Lanka as a good investment station," he said.
